newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares surge on tranche merger rumours.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares surge on tranche merger rumours.

text.p: A 62-point surge of the Straits Times Industrials Index on Friday left dealers calling for Singapore firms with domestic and foreign shares tranches to make a definitive statement about possible plans to merge them.
"The speculation about this has created a volatility in the market that is very unnerving for investors. The issue needs to be resolved one way or another," a dealer at a local firm said.
The STII rocketed 62.03 to 1,953.80 by Friday's close, reversing a week of falls, but dealers said the climb was not representative of real market sentiment.
"The jump is on the back of a handful of shares. The other indicators don't show the same enthusiasm," another dealer said.
Out of an active trading day of 260 million shares, losers swamped gainers 264 to 135.

The STII took off after rumours in the market that the goverment might scrap a system of dual share listings for strategic blue chip companies. Domestic tranches can be bought only by Singaporeans. Foreign tranches are open to all buyers.
State-owned Singapore Technologies added grist to the rumour mill by announcing on Wednesday it would end the dual listings of its units after a move last week to merge the tranches of just one.
Dealers said while some overseas buyers had been able to cash in their chips, others now had their hands tied, unable to get out after significant falls of foreign tranches.
One dealer said his clients "have lost Singapore $10 million today, but it's not my fault. It's all to do with policy."
Foreign stock of Singapore Press Holdings saw 10 percent, or Singapore $2.70, wiped off its value to end at an even S$22.00. DBS Bank foreign lost S$1.20 to S$15.80.
Singapore Airlines foreign and UOB Bank both fell S$0.60 to S$11.00 and S$12.30 respectively.

Conversely, the domestic tranches shot up. SPH gained S$1.50 to S$14.90 -- cranking the STII up 24 points along with it. DBS rose S$0.55 to S$10.40 and UOB and SIA climed S$0.45 apiece to S$9.60 and S$8.45 respectively.
Top active was debut share Amara Holdings, which closed at S$0.46 against its offer price of S$0.30.
